why: The estate had a process for ownership (claims, heartbeats, the collision check) and a process for code (gates, CI, Greenlane) and no process for truth: nothing standing said whether the founder's own path answered. Every predicate here is a question about the founder's real path, and every one of them is answered with MEASURED_OK, MEASURED_FAIL or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is never OK.
rules: A predicate's verdict is about its ANSWER, never about the connect: a path that refuses the connection has been measured, and it did not work.

A credential that is absent from this host does not stop the measurement. The path is asked anyway; a refusal is MEASURED_FAIL and a success without the credential is UNKNOWN (the endpoint answers, the founder's credentialed path is not proven).

The aggregate verdict is total over the predicates THIS host can measure: any MEASURED_FAIL makes it MEASURED_FAIL, any UNKNOWN makes it UNKNOWN, and only an all-OK set is MEASURED_OK. There is no path by which the estate is reported healthy by omission.

A predicate this host cannot measure at all -- a cluster question asked from a laptop -- is reported separately, by name, as out of scope, and it does not count against the verdict here. A board that can never be green teaches the estate to ignore the board. The total verdict over every predicate is published beside the host verdict as verdict_all, so the split hides nothing.

The router's lane ledger carries two shapes: a bare lane name and a refusal record such as {'lane': 'glm', 'reason': '...', 'verdict': '...'}. Both are read. One unhashable dict must not be able to take the whole board down.
No predicate may print a credential, a prompt body or a response body. The probe prompt is the fixed string 'Reply with exactly: PONG' and the expected token is PONG.
